**EL-RSP-1 Direction-indicator response time and phase**

When the turn stalk or the hazard warning button changes state, every affected direction-indicator lamp shall show the change within 200 ms.

The front and rear lamps of one side shall change state no more than 80 ms apart, so that they are seen to flash in phase.

description: Top-level requirement on ExteriorLightingDesign. 200 ms keeps the lamps and telltale in step with the driver's hand on the stalk; UN R48 asks for the lamps of one side to flash in phase, and its own 1 s switch-on limit is met with a wide margin.
Refined by RationaleClaim_NonSafety_ExteriorLightingDesign_IndicatorResponseTime into a time budget along the signal path (EL_Indicator_Response_Time_Analysis.md):
| stalk or button to DriverCan0 frame | EL-RSP-1.1 SCCM_Lighting | ≤ 50 ms |
| input frame to TurnLightControl sent | EL-RSP-1.2 BCM_Lighting | ≤ 60 ms |
| TurnLightControl to front lamp | EL-RSP-1.3 FLCM_Lighting | 10–20 ms |
| TurnLightControl to rear lamp | EL-RSP-1.4 RearLight | 10–65 ms |
The parts of these budgets the platform delivers are allocated further to DriverCan0, BodyCan0, RearLightLIN, BCM_ECU and RLCM_ECU.
